vocab.definition: to become weaker or less intense; to die down
vocab.example: The storm finally began to abate after midnight.

vocab.definition: different from what is normal or accepted; abnormal
vocab.example: The lab reran the test because one result was clearly aberrant.

vocab.definition: quick and cheerful eagerness; readiness
vocab.example: She accepted the invitation with alacrity.

vocab.definition: to make a bad situation better; to improve
vocab.example: The new policy was meant to ameliorate conditions in overcrowded schools.

vocab.definition: an unusual case that does not fit the normal pattern; an irregularity
vocab.example: A warm day in the middle of a cold winter is an anomaly.

vocab.definition: to calm or ease an unpleasant feeling; to soothe
vocab.example: Nothing the doctor said could assuage his fears.

vocab.definition: willing to take bold risks; daring
vocab.example: The startup's audacious plan surprised even its investors.

vocab.definition: strict and serious; also, plain and without decoration
vocab.example: The monks lived in austere rooms with no furniture but a bed.

vocab.definition: dull and unoriginal; commonplace
vocab.example: The film's dialogue was so banal that the audience laughed at it.

vocab.definition: to give a false idea of something; to contradict
vocab.example: His relaxed smile belied the stress he was under.

vocab.definition: to support or strengthen
vocab.example: New data bolstered the researchers' hypothesis.

vocab.definition: the quality of being open and honest; frankness
vocab.example: I appreciated the candor of her feedback.

vocab.definition: changing mood or behavior suddenly, for no reason; unpredictable
vocab.example: The team struggled under a capricious manager who changed priorities daily.

vocab.definition: to criticize or scold severely; to rebuke
vocab.example: The editorial castigated the government for its slow response.

vocab.definition: clear, logical, and convincing
vocab.example: She made a cogent case for extending the deadline.

vocab.definition: meant to make peace or calm anger; peacemaking
vocab.example: After the argument, he sent a conciliatory message.

vocab.definition: to confirm a statement or theory with evidence; to back up
vocab.example: Two witnesses corroborated the driver's account.

vocab.definition: to express contempt for; to ridicule
vocab.example: Critics derided the proposal as unrealistic.

vocab.definition: an angry, bitter verbal attack; a rant
vocab.example: The speech turned into a diatribe against the media.

vocab.definition: shy because of a lack of self-confidence; timid
vocab.example: The diffident student rarely spoke in class.

vocab.definition: very different from each other; unlike
vocab.example: The book connects disparate fields such as biology and economics.

vocab.definition: insisting that one's opinions are true beyond question; rigid
vocab.example: His dogmatic attitude made discussion impossible.

vocab.definition: taking ideas or styles from many different sources; varied
vocab.example: Her playlist is eclectic, mixing jazz, samba and metal.

vocab.definition: the ability to produce the intended result; effectiveness
vocab.example: Trials are testing the efficacy of the new vaccine.

vocab.definition: to make someone feel weak and tired; to drain
vocab.example: The heat enervated the hikers. (Atenção: NÃO significa 'energizar'.)

vocab.definition: lasting a very short time; fleeting
vocab.example: Social media fame is often ephemeral.

vocab.definition: to avoid giving a clear answer on purpose; to hedge
vocab.example: When asked about the budget, the minister equivocated.

vocab.definition: having great knowledge from study; learned
vocab.example: The professor gave an erudite lecture on medieval law.

vocab.definition: to make a problem or bad situation worse; to aggravate
vocab.example: Cutting staff would only exacerbate the delays.

vocab.definition: to praise very highly; to glorify
vocab.example: The review extolled the restaurant's desserts.

vocab.definition: very careful about accuracy and detail; hard to please
vocab.example: A fastidious editor, she checked every comma.

vocab.definition: talking too much, especially about unimportant things; chatty
vocab.example: The garrulous passenger talked for the entire flight.

vocab.definition: fond of company; sociable
vocab.example: Gregarious people often enjoy working in teams.

vocab.definition: used so often that it is no longer interesting; clichéd
vocab.example: The essay was full of hackneyed expressions.

vocab.definition: a person who attacks traditional beliefs or institutions; a rebel
vocab.example: As an iconoclast, the economist challenged every accepted model.

vocab.definition: acting quickly without thinking; rash
vocab.example: His impetuous decision to quit cost him dearly.

vocab.definition: not harmful or offensive; harmless
vocab.example: What seemed an innocuous comment upset the client.

vocab.definition: using very few words; brief
vocab.example: Her laconic reply was simply 'No.'

vocab.definition: to praise highly, especially in public
vocab.example: The mayor lauded the volunteers for their work.

vocab.definition: to make something less severe or painful; to lessen
vocab.example: Planting trees can mitigate the effects of urban heat.

vocab.definition: stubbornly refusing to change one's mind; unyielding
vocab.example: The obdurate landlord refused every request for repairs.

vocab.definition: too eager to please or obey; servile
vocab.example: The obsequious waiter laughed at all of the manager's jokes.

vocab.definition: impossible to see through; also, hard to understand
vocab.example: The contract's language was deliberately opaque.

vocab.definition: a lack of something; scarcity
vocab.example: A paucity of data made the conclusion uncertain.

vocab.definition: done quickly, with little care or effort; routine
vocab.example: He gave the report a perfunctory glance and signed it.

vocab.definition: to make an angry person calmer; to pacify
vocab.example: The company offered refunds to placate angry customers.

vocab.definition: dealing with things sensibly and realistically; practical
vocab.example: We need a pragmatic solution, not a perfect one.

vocab.definition: spending money or resources wastefully; extravagant
vocab.example: The prodigal heir spent his fortune in two years.

vocab.definition: a natural tendency to behave in a certain way; inclination
vocab.example: He has a propensity to exaggerate.

vocab.definition: ordinary and unimaginative; dull
vocab.example: The truth behind the legend was quite prosaic.

vocab.definition: quiet and inactive for a time; dormant
vocab.example: The volcano has been quiescent for centuries.

vocab.definition: refusing to obey rules or authority; uncooperative
vocab.example: The recalcitrant student ignored every warning.

vocab.definition: unwilling to share one's thoughts or feelings; reserved
vocab.example: She was reticent about her plans after graduation.

vocab.definition: official approval; also, a penalty for breaking a rule
vocab.example: The trip had the sanction of the school board. (Palavra com dois sentidos opostos.)

vocab.definition: causing sleepiness; sleep-inducing
vocab.example: The lecturer's soporific voice put half the class to sleep.

vocab.definition: understood without being said; unspoken
vocab.example: There was a tacit agreement not to discuss politics at dinner.

vocab.definition: very weak or thin; flimsy
vocab.example: The link between the two events is tenuous.

vocab.definition: to keep changing between opinions or choices; to waver
vocab.example: She vacillated between studying law and medicine.

vocab.definition: to respect someone or something deeply; to revere
vocab.example: The scientist is venerated by her former students.

vocab.definition: showing great energy and enthusiasm for a cause; passionate
vocab.example: The zealous volunteers worked through the night.

vocabSentences.sentence: Although the senator's speech was praised for its ___ reasoning, critics noted that it relied on a single outdated study.
vocabSentences.explanation: 'Although' opõe o elogio à crítica; o elogio pede algo positivo sobre o raciocínio: cogent (convincente).
vocabSentences.explanationEn: 'Although' sets the praise against the criticism; the praise calls for something positive about the reasoning: cogent (convincing).

vocabSentences.sentence: The new manager's ___ approach surprised the staff, who had expected someone far more cautious.
vocabSentences.explanation: O contraste com 'far more cautious' pede 'ousado': audacious e daring formam frases equivalentes.
vocabSentences.explanationEn: The contrast with 'far more cautious' calls for 'bold': audacious and daring produce equivalent sentences.

vocabSentences.sentence: Far from ___ the tension, the mediator's blunt remarks only intensified it.
vocabSentences.explanation: 'Far from X… only intensified' = X é o oposto de intensificar: assuaging (aliviar).
vocabSentences.explanationEn: 'Far from X… only intensified' = X is the opposite of intensifying: assuaging (easing).

vocabSentences.sentence: Her calm voice ___ the panic she felt; no one in the audience suspected how nervous she was.
vocabSentences.explanation: Ninguém percebeu o nervosismo, então a voz escondeu o pânico: belied e masked. Revealed/betrayed é o par-armadilha (sentido oposto).
vocabSentences.explanationEn: Nobody noticed the nervousness, so the voice hid the panic: belied and masked. Revealed/betrayed is the trap pair (opposite meaning).

vocabSentences.sentence: Visitors found the exhibition ___: it combined Renaissance portraits, street art and video installations.
vocabSentences.explanation: Os dois-pontos explicam a palavra: fontes muito variadas = eclectic.
vocabSentences.explanationEn: The colon explains the word: very varied sources = eclectic.

vocabSentences.sentence: The fame of most viral videos is ___; within a week, few people remember them.
vocabSentences.explanation: 'Em uma semana ninguém lembra' = dura pouco: ephemeral e fleeting.
vocabSentences.explanationEn: 'Within a week nobody remembers' = short-lived: ephemeral and fleeting.

vocabSentences.sentence: Rather than offering a clear answer, the spokesperson continued to ___, leaving reporters more confused than before.
vocabSentences.explanation: 'Rather than a clear answer' + repórteres confusos = falar de forma ambígua: equivocate.
vocabSentences.explanationEn: 'Rather than a clear answer' + confused reporters = speaking ambiguously: equivocate.

vocabSentences.sentence: Cutting the maintenance budget will only ___ the problems with the city's aging bridges.
vocabSentences.explanation: 'Will only ___ the problems' com corte de verba = piorar: exacerbate e aggravate.
vocabSentences.explanationEn: 'Will only ___ the problems' with a budget cut = make worse: exacerbate and aggravate.

vocabSentences.sentence: Known for his ___ replies, the coach rarely said more than a few words to reporters.
vocabSentences.explanation: 'Rarely said more than a few words' define laconic. Garrulous é o oposto.
vocabSentences.explanationEn: 'Rarely said more than a few words' defines laconic. Garrulous is the opposite.

vocabSentences.sentence: Despite the new evidence, the committee remained ___, refusing to reconsider its decision.
vocabSentences.explanation: 'Refusing to reconsider' = inflexível: obdurate e adamant.
vocabSentences.explanationEn: 'Refusing to reconsider' = inflexible: obdurate and adamant.

vocabSentences.sentence: The inspector's review was so ___ that she missed several obvious safety violations.
vocabSentences.explanation: Deixar passar problemas óbvios = revisão feita sem cuidado: perfunctory. Fastidious seria o contrário.
vocabSentences.explanationEn: Missing obvious problems = a careless review: perfunctory. Fastidious would be the opposite.

vocabSentences.sentence: The speech was full of ___ phrases such as 'think outside the box', which bored the audience.
vocabSentences.explanation: O exemplo é um clichê que entediou o público: hackneyed e clichéd.
vocabSentences.explanationEn: The example is a cliché that bored the audience: hackneyed and clichéd.

vocabSentences.sentence: The lecture was so ___ that several students struggled to stay awake.
vocabSentences.explanation: 'Struggled to stay awake' = que dá sono: soporific.

vocabSentences.sentence: The connection between the two events is ___ at best; the evidence linking them is extremely thin.
vocabSentences.explanation: 'Evidence extremely thin' = ligação fraca: tenuous e flimsy.
vocabSentences.explanationEn: 'Evidence extremely thin' = weak link: tenuous and flimsy.

vocabSentences.sentence: The partners never signed a contract, but they had a ___ agreement that each would cover half the costs.
vocabSentences.explanation: Acordo existente sem nada escrito ou dito = tacit.
vocabSentences.explanationEn: An existing agreement with nothing written or said = tacit.

vocabSentences.sentence: Unable to choose between the two job offers, Marta continued to ___ for weeks.
vocabSentences.explanation: 'Unable to choose' = hesitar entre opções: vacillate e waver.
vocabSentences.explanationEn: 'Unable to choose' = hesitate between options: vacillate and waver.

options: The relationship cannot be determined from the information given

quant.solution: 0.9² = 0.81. Número entre 0 e 1 elevado ao quadrado diminui.
quant.solutionEn: 0.9² = 0.81. Squaring a number between 0 and 1 makes it smaller.

quant.prompt: If 3x − 7 = 11, what is the value of x?
The price of a jacket is increased by 20% and then the new price is decreased by 20%. The final price is what percent of the original price?
A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 and a length of 9. What is its area?
How many integers from 10 to 50, inclusive, are divisible by 6?
A right triangle has legs of length 6 and 8. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
If 2^x = 32, what is the value of 2^(x − 2)?
The average of five numbers is 12. Four of the numbers are 10, 14, 9 and 15. What is the fifth number?
Pipe A fills a tank in 3 hours and pipe B fills it in 6 hours. Working together, how many hours do they take to fill the tank?
quant.solutionEn: 1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2 of the tank per hour → 2 hours.

quant.prompt: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability that both land heads? (Give a fraction or decimal.)
A car travels 150 kilometers in 2.5 hours at a constant speed. What is its speed, in kilometers per hour?

prompts.statement: Governments should place few, if any, restrictions on scientific research and development.
prompts.instructions: Write a response in which you discuss the extent to which you agree or disagree with the recommendation and explain your reasoning for the position you take. In developing and supporting your position, describe specific circumstances in which adopting the recommendation would or would not be advantageous and explain how these examples shape your position.

prompts.statement: The best way to teach is to praise positive actions and ignore negative ones.

buildSentence.note: 10 itens, 1 ponto cada; tempo próprio não informado no material oficial (o resto da seção de ~23 min).

practice.context: Why were you late this morning?
practice.answer: The bus that I usually take did not come.

practice.context: Are you joining the study group tonight?
practice.answer: Do you know where the group is meeting?

practice.context: I just moved to a new apartment.
practice.answer: How far is it from the university?

practice.context: What did the professor say about the exam?
practice.answer: She told us that it would cover the first five chapters.
Could you tell me what time the first session begins?

buildSentence.noteEn: 10 items, 1 point each; no separate time limit in the official material (it shares the ~23-min section).

practice.situation: You signed up for a weekend photography course at your local community center. Yesterday, the center moved the class from Saturday morning to Thursday evening, when you have to work.
practice.subject: Schedule change for the photography course
bullets: Explain why you signed up for the course.
Describe the problem the schedule change causes for you.

practice.situation: Last week a classmate lent you an expensive textbook. While you were studying at a café, you spilled coffee on it and several pages were damaged.
practice.subject: About your textbook
bullets: Suggest a time and place to meet.

practice.professor: Your professor is teaching a class on urban planning. Professor: Many cities in Europe have turned their historic centers into pedestrian-only zones. Supporters say this makes cities cleaner and safer; opponents say it hurts businesses and makes life harder for some residents. Should cities ban private cars from their central areas? Why or why not?

students.name: Ana
students.post: Yes. Car-free centers have less pollution and fewer accidents. When my city closed its main avenue to cars on Sundays, local shops were actually busier because people walked around more.

students.name: Kevin
students.post: I disagree. Elderly people and people with disabilities depend on cars, and shops still need deliveries. A total ban would make the center less accessible, not more.

practice.professor: Your professor is teaching a class on business management. Professor: Several companies have experimented with a four-day workweek while keeping salaries the same. Should more companies adopt a four-day workweek? Why or why not?

students.name: Priya
students.post: I think so. Rested employees are more focused, and companies that tried it reported similar productivity with fewer sick days.

students.name: Lucas
students.post: It depends on the industry. A hospital or a customer support center can't just close one day a week, so it might be unfair or impossible for many workers.

practice.scenario: You are training to give campus tours. Listen to your supervisor and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.
sentences: The library is on your left.
Students can borrow laptops at the front desk.
The cafeteria closes at eight on weekdays and at six on weekends.
If you lose your ID card, report it to the security office right away.
The building that you see across the street was designed by a former student.
Visitors who would like to attend a lecture should register online at least one day in advance.

practice.scenario: You are volunteering at a science museum. Listen to the coordinator and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.
sentences: Tickets are sold at the main entrance.
Please keep your bags in the lockers.
The dinosaur exhibit is on the second floor.
Photography is allowed, but please turn off your flash.
Guided tours start every hour and last about forty minutes.
Children under twelve must be accompanied by an adult at all times.
The planetarium show, which was updated last year, explains how stars are formed.

practice.scenario: You have agreed to take part in a research study about technology and learning. A researcher will ask you some questions.
questions: Do you usually study alone, with friends, or online? Tell me a little about how you study.
Some people learn best by watching videos, while others prefer reading. Which do you prefer, and why?
Some people think universities should replace most lectures with online courses. Do you agree? Why or why not?
Researchers predict that AI tutors will become common in the next ten years. Do you think this will improve education? Why or why not?

practice.scenario: You have agreed to take part in a study about transportation and work. A researcher will ask you some questions.
questions: How do you usually get to work or school?
What is one thing you would change about public transportation where you live? Why?
Some companies let employees work from home permanently. Do you think this is a good idea? Why or why not?
Some cities are considering charging drivers a fee to enter the city center during busy hours. Do you think this policy would be effective? Why or why not?

rubricRepeat.4: Meaning captured; minor changes (1–2 function words, a related content word, tense/number markers)
rubricRepeat.3: Essentially full, but original meaning not accurately captured
rubricRepeat.2: Significant part missing and/or highly inaccurate
rubricRepeat.1: Very little of the prompt, or largely unintelligible
rubricRepeat.0: No response / unintelligible / not English / unrelated

rubricInterview.5: On topic, well elaborated; good pace; easily intelligible; range of accurate grammar and vocabulary
rubricInterview.4: On topic and elaborated (may lack connectors); generally good pace; occasional words need minor effort; grammar/vocabulary adequate most of the time
rubricInterview.3: Generally on topic, limited elaboration; choppy pace, frequent fillers; intelligibility sometimes affected; limited range
rubricInterview.2: Minimally connected; little relevant elaboration; limited intelligibility
rubricInterview.1: Only vaguely connected; mostly unintelligible; isolated words
rubricInterview.0: No response / unintelligible / not English / unrelated
